1	"""Named branches over a shared event graph."""
2	
3	from __future__ import annotations
4	
5	import math
6	from typing import Any
7	
8	from city_twin.event_graph import EventGraph
9	
10	
11	class BranchStore:
12	    """Named heads into a shared :class:`EventGraph`.
13	
14	    A branch is created from an existing event and grows only by appending
15	    events whose sole parent is the branch's current head, so branches
16	    never move each other's heads. Appends are idempotent: the store
17	    records the ``(at, changes)`` each branch appended under an event id,
18	    and repeating the same call is a no-op. All validation finishes before
19	    any state is touched, so a failed call leaves the graph, branch heads
20	    and idempotency records unchanged.
21	    """
22	
23	    def __init__(self, graph: EventGraph) -> None:
24	        if not isinstance(graph, EventGraph):
25	            raise TypeError(
26	                f"graph must be an EventGraph, got {type(graph).__name__}"
27	            )
28	        self._graph = graph
29	        self._heads: dict[str, str] = {}
30	        self._sources: dict[str, str] = {}
31	        self._appends: dict[str, dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, int]]]] = {}
32	        self._merges: dict[str, tuple[str, str, int, dict[str, int]]] = {}
33	
34	    @staticmethod
35	    def _require_nonempty_str(value: Any, name: str) -> None:
36	        # Same contract as EventGraph.add's string parameters.
37	        EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(value, name)
38	
39	    def _require_known_branch(self, name: str) -> None:
40	        if name not in self._heads:
41	            raise KeyError(name)
42	
43	    def create(self, name: str, from_event: str) -> None:
44	        """Create a branch named ``name`` starting at ``from_event``.
45	
46	        Re-creating with the same name and source is a no-op; the same
47	        name with a different source is a conflict.
48	        """
49	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
50	        self._require_nonempty_str(from_event, "from_event")
51	
52	        if name in self._heads:
53	            if self._sources[name] != from_event:
54	                raise ValueError(
55	                    f"branch {name!r} already exists from "
56	                    f"{self._sources[name]!r}, not {from_event!r}"
57	                )
58	            return
59	        if from_event not in self._graph._at:
60	            raise KeyError(from_event)
61	
62	        self._heads[name] = from_event
63	        self._sources[name] = from_event
64	        self._appends[name] = {}
65	
66	    def append(
67	        self,
68	        name: str,
69	        id: str,
70	        at: int,
71	        changes: dict[str, int],
72	    ) -> None:
73	        """Append an event whose sole parent is the branch's current head.
74	
75	        The head moves only if :meth:`EventGraph.add` succeeds. Repeating
76	        an append with the same ``name``/``id``/``at``/``changes`` is a
77	        no-op; reusing ``id`` with different inputs is a conflict, here
78	        and via the graph across branches.
79	        """
80	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
81	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
82	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
83	        # The at/changes contract is exactly EventGraph.add's.
84	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
85	        if at_value < 0:
86	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
87	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
88	            raise TypeError(
89	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
90	            )
91	        for key, value in changes.items():
92	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
93	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
94	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
95	        changes = dict(changes)
96	
97	        self._require_known_branch(name)
98	
99	        recorded = self._appends[name].get(id)
100	        if recorded is not None:
101	            if recorded == (at_value, changes):
102	                return
103	            raise ValueError(
104	                f"event {id!r} already appended on branch {name!r} "
105	                f"with different inputs"
106	            )
107	
108	        head = self._heads[name]
109	        self._graph.add(id, at_value, (head,), changes)
110	
111	        # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
112	        self._heads[name] = id
113	        self._appends[name][id] = (at_value, changes)
114	
115	    def merge(
116	        self,
117	        target: str,
118	        source: str,
119	        id: str,
120	        at: int,
121	        changes: dict[str, int],
122	    ) -> None:
123	        """Merge ``source`` into ``target`` under a new two-parent event.
124	
125	        The event's parents are ordered ``(target head, source head)``;
126	        only the target head moves, the source head is untouched. Calls
127	        are idempotent on the exact five-tuple, and reusing ``id`` with
128	        different inputs (here or in the graph) is a conflict. A merge is
129	        rejected when events exclusive to either side touch overlapping
130	        change keys. All validation finishes before any state is touched,
131	        so a failed call leaves the graph, heads and records unchanged.
132	        """
133	        # --- Full validation happens before any state is consulted. ---
134	        self._require_nonempty_str(target, "target")
135	        self._require_nonempty_str(source, "source")
136	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
137	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
138	        if at_value < 0:
139	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")
140	        if not isinstance(changes, dict):
141	            raise TypeError(
142	                f"changes must be a dict, got {type(changes).__name__}"
143	            )
144	        for key, value in changes.items():
145	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "change key")
146	            EventGraph._require_int(value, f"change value for {key!r}")
147	        # Copy caller-owned input before it can be recorded anywhere.
148	        changes = dict(changes)
149	
150	        self._require_known_branch(target)
151	        self._require_known_branch(source)
152	        if target == source:
153	            raise ValueError(f"cannot merge branch {target!r} into itself")
154	
155	        recorded = self._merges.get(id)
156	        if recorded is not None:
157	            if recorded == (target, source, at_value, changes):
158	                return
159	            raise ValueError(
160	                f"merge event {id!r} already recorded with different inputs"
161	            )
162	
163	        target_head = self._heads[target]
164	        source_head = self._heads[source]
165	
166	        target_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(target_head))
167	        source_closure = set(self._graph._ordered_ancestors(source_head))
168	        common = target_closure & source_closure
169	
170	        target_keys: set[str] = set()
171	        for event_id in target_closure - common:
172	            target_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
173	        source_keys: set[str] = set()
174	        for event_id in source_closure - common:
175	            source_keys.update(self._graph._changes[event_id])
176	        overlap = target_keys & source_keys
177	        if overlap:
178	            raise ValueError(
179	                "conflicting changes on keys: "
180	                + ", ".join(sorted(overlap))
181	            )
182	
183	        self._graph.add(id, at_value, (target_head, source_head), changes)
184	
185	        # --- Commit: only after the graph accepted the event. ---
186	        self._heads[target] = id
187	        self._merges[id] = (target, source, at_value, changes)
188	
189	    def audit_merge(self, id: str) -> dict[str, object]:
190	        """Return an audit record for the merge event ``id``.
191	
192	        The record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
193	        ``event_id, target, source, parents, at, changes``: the merge
194	        event id, the target and source branch names, the recorded
195	        parent ids (target head first), the non-negative timestamp and
196	        a copy of the merged changes. Unknown ids and ids of non-merge
197	        events raise :class:`KeyError`; mutating the returned dict or
198	        its ``changes`` never affects the store's records.
199	        """
200	        self._require_nonempty_str(id, "id")
201	        recorded = self._merges.get(id)
202	        if recorded is None:
203	            raise KeyError(id)
204	        target, source, at_value, changes = recorded
205	        return {
206	            "event_id": id,
207	            "target": target,
208	            "source": source,
209	            "parents": self._graph._parents[id],
210	            "at": at_value,
211	            "changes": dict(changes),
212	        }
213	
214	    def audit_log(self) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
215	        """Return audit records for every event this store recorded.
216	
217	        Covers exactly the branch appends and merges performed through
218	        this store -- events added directly to the graph are not
219	        included -- each exactly once, ordered by ``(at, event_id)``
220	        ascending (event ids compared by Unicode code point). Each
221	        record is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
222	        ``event_id, kind, owner, peer, parents, at, changes``: for an
223	        append, ``owner`` is the branch name, ``peer`` is ``None`` and
224	        ``parents`` is the single-element parent id tuple; for a merge,
225	        ``owner`` is the target branch, ``peer`` is the source branch
226	        and ``parents`` is the two-element tuple with the target parent
227	        first. ``changes`` is a copy ordered by Unicode code point of
228	        its keys. The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and
229	        records are never modified, and the returned tuple, dicts and
230	        changes are detached from internal state, so mutating them
231	        affects neither the store nor later calls, and repeated calls
232	        return item-wise equal results in a stable order.
233	        """
234	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
235	        for name, appends in self._appends.items():
236	            for event_id, (at_value, changes) in appends.items():
237	                records.append(
238	                    {
239	                        "event_id": event_id,
240	                        "kind": "append",
241	                        "owner": name,
242	                        "peer": None,
243	                        "parents": self._graph._parents[event_id],
244	                        "at": at_value,
245	                        "changes": {
246	                            key: changes[key] for key in sorted(changes)
247	                        },
248	                    }
249	                )
250	        for event_id, (target, source, at_value, changes) in (
251	            self._merges.items()
252	        ):
253	            records.append(
254	                {
255	                    "event_id": event_id,
256	                    "kind": "merge",
257	                    "owner": target,
258	                    "peer": source,
259	                    "parents": self._graph._parents[event_id],
260	                    "at": at_value,
261	                    "changes": {
262	                        key: changes[key] for key in sorted(changes)
263	                    },
264	                }
265	            )
266	        records.sort(
267	            key=lambda record: (record["at"], record["event_id"])
268	        )
269	        return tuple(records)
270	
271	    def trace(self, name: str, key: str) -> tuple[str, ...]:
272	        """Return ids of events on ``name``'s head closure touching ``key``.
273	
274	        Ids follow the graph's replay order and include zero-delta and
275	        merge events, each at most once.
276	        """
277	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
278	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
279	        self._require_known_branch(name)
280	        return self._graph.explain(self._heads[name], key)
281	
282	    def explain_change(
283	        self, name: str, key: str
284	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
285	        """Explain the causal value trajectory of ``key`` on a branch.
286	
287	        The branch's current head ancestor closure is replayed in the
288	        graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order. Every event
289	        whose changes contain ``key`` -- including zero-delta and merge
290	        events -- appears exactly once, with the key's integer value
291	        accumulated from an initial ``0``. Each record is a fresh dict
292	        whose keys are ordered ``event_id, at, parents, delta, before,
293	        after``: the event id, its non-negative timestamp, a copy of its
294	        recorded parent ids (for a merge, target head first, source head
295	        second), the integer delta the event applies to ``key`` and the
296	        values immediately before and after applying it. ``name`` and
297	        ``key`` are validated (in that order) before the branch is looked
298	        up: non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty strings
299	        raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
300	        :class:`KeyError`. The query is read-only and its result is
301	        detached from internal state, so the graph, branch heads, audit
302	        and idempotency records are never modified, and repeated calls
303	        return item-wise equal results.
304	        """
305	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
306	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
307	        self._require_known_branch(name)
308	
309	        order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name])
310	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
311	        value = 0
312	        for event_id in order:
313	            changes = self._graph._changes[event_id]
314	            if key not in changes:
315	                continue
316	            delta = changes[key]
317	            before = value
318	            value += delta
319	            records.append(
320	                {
321	                    "event_id": event_id,
322	                    "at": self._graph._at[event_id],
323	                    "parents": (*self._graph._parents[event_id],),
324	                    "delta": delta,
325	                    "before": before,
326	                    "after": value,
327	                }
328	            )
329	        return tuple(records)
330	
331	    def explain_impact(
332	        self, name: str, event_id: str
333	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
334	        """Explain the forward causal impact of an event on a branch.
335	
336	        Within the ancestor closure of the branch's current head, edges
337	        point parent-to-child as the impact direction. The strict
338	        descendants of ``event_id`` -- reachable events other than
339	        ``event_id`` itself -- are returned each exactly once, in the
340	        graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order. Each record
341	        is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``event_id, at, path,
342	        keys``: the descendant id, its non-negative timestamp, the tuple
343	        of ids on the shortest path from ``event_id`` to it (both ends
344	        included), and the tuple of change keys its ``changes`` touch,
345	        sorted by Unicode code point (an empty tuple for events with no
346	        changes). When several paths exist, the one with the fewest edges
347	        wins, ties broken by the Unicode code point order of the complete
348	        id tuples; no descendants yields an empty tuple. ``name`` and
349	        ``event_id`` are validated (in that order) before the branch is
350	        looked up: non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty
351	        strings raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
352	        :class:`KeyError`, and an ``event_id`` absent from the graph or
353	        outside the branch's current head ancestor closure raises
354	        :class:`KeyError`. The query is read-only and its result is
355	        detached from internal state, so the graph, branch heads, audit
356	        and idempotency records are never modified, and repeated calls
357	        return item-wise equal results.
358	        """
359	        self._require_nonempty_str(name, "name")
360	        self._require_nonempty_str(event_id, "event_id")
361	        self._require_known_branch(name)
362	        if event_id not in self._graph._at:
363	            raise KeyError(event_id)
364	
365	        head = self._heads[name]
366	        order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(head)
367	        closure = set(order)
368	        if event_id not in closure:
369	            raise KeyError(event_id)
370	
371	        # Reverse the parent edges within the closure so children can be
372	        # enumerated parent-to-child.
373	        children: dict[str, list[str]] = {event: [] for event in closure}
374	        for current in closure:
375	            for parent in self._graph._parents[current]:
376	                children[parent].append(current)
377	
378	        # Level-by-level breadth-first search gives the fewest-edge
379	        # paths. Within a level every candidate path has equal length, so
380	        # keeping the minimum full id tuple applies the Unicode code
381	        # point tie-break; children are claimed only after the whole
382	        # level is evaluated, so every shortest candidate is compared.
383	        paths: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {event_id: (event_id,)}
384	        frontier = [event_id]
385	        while frontier:
386	            candidates: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {}
387	            for current in frontier:
388	                current_path = paths[current]
389	                for child in children[current]:
390	                    if child in paths:
391	                        continue
392	                    candidate = (*current_path, child)
393	                    best = candidates.get(child)
394	                    if best is None or candidate < best:
395	                        candidates[child] = candidate
396	            for child, path in candidates.items():
397	                paths[child] = path
398	            frontier = list(candidates)
399	
400	        # Descendants are reported in the closure's existing replay
401	        # order: parents before children, ready events by (at, id).
402	        records: list[dict[str, object]] = []
403	        for descendant in order:
404	            if descendant == event_id or descendant not in paths:
405	                continue
406	            changes = self._graph._changes[descendant]
407	            records.append(
408	                {
409	                    "event_id": descendant,
410	                    "at": self._graph._at[descendant],
411	                    "path": (*paths[descendant],),
412	                    "keys": tuple(sorted(changes)),
413	                }
414	            )
415	        return tuple(records)

417	    def diff_at(self, name_a: str, name_b: str, at: int) -> dict[str, tuple[int, int]]:
418	        """Diff two branches' current heads as of ``at``.

420	        Both names and ``at`` are validated (in signature order) before
421	        either branch is looked up; the diff itself is delegated to
422	        :meth:`EventGraph.diff_at` on the branches' current heads. The
423	        query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
424	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
425	        from internal state.
426	        """
427	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
428	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
429	        at_value = EventGraph._require_int(at, "at")
430	        if at_value < 0:
431	            raise ValueError("at must be a non-negative int")

433	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)

438	    def compare(self, name_a: str, name_b: str) -> dict[str, object]:
439	        """Compare the ancestor closures of two branches' current heads.
440	
441	        Both names are validated (in signature order) before either
442	        branch is looked up: non-``str`` names raise :class:`TypeError`,
443	        empty names raise :class:`ValueError`, unknown branches raise
444	        :class:`KeyError`, and comparing a branch with itself raises
445	        :class:`ValueError`. Each head's ancestor closure is taken once,
446	        in the graph's parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` replay
447	        order. The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
448	        ``common, left_only, right_only, fork``: tuples of event ids for
449	        the intersection, the left-only and the right-only events
450	        (common and left-only in left replay order, right-only in right
451	        replay order), plus ``fork`` -- the last common id in left replay
452	        order, or ``None`` when the closures share no event. The query
453	        is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are never
454	        modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached from
455	        internal state.
456	        """
457	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
458	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
459	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
460	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
461	        if name_a == name_b:
462	            raise ValueError(f"cannot compare branch {name_a!r} with itself")
463	
464	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
465	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
466	        left_ids = set(left_order)
467	        right_ids = set(right_order)
468	
469	        common = tuple(
470	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id in right_ids
471	        )
472	        left_only = tuple(
473	            event_id for event_id in left_order if event_id not in right_ids
474	        )
475	        right_only = tuple(
476	            event_id for event_id in right_order if event_id not in left_ids
477	        )
478	        return {
479	            "common": common,
480	            "left_only": left_only,
481	            "right_only": right_only,
482	            "fork": common[-1] if common else None,
483	        }

485	    def attribute_divergence(
486	        self, name_a: str, name_b: str, key: str
487	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
488	        """Attribute the cross-branch divergence of ``key`` to its causes.
489	
490	        Both names and ``key`` are validated (in signature order) before
491	        either branch is looked up: non-``str`` values raise
492	        :class:`TypeError`, empty strings raise :class:`ValueError`,
493	        unknown branches raise :class:`KeyError` (``name_a`` first), and
494	        naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`. Each
495	        branch's current head ancestor closure is replayed in the graph's
496	        parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order; a side on which
497	        ``key`` never appears contributes the value ``0``.
498	
499	        The result is a fresh dict whose keys are ordered
500	        ``key, fork, left, right``: ``key`` is the queried key as given
501	        and ``fork`` is the last common event id in left replay order (or
502	        ``None`` when the closures share no event). ``left`` and ``right``
503	        are fresh dicts whose keys are ordered ``value, cause, path,
504	        affected``: the replayed integer value, the cause event id, and
505	        data derived from it. When the two values differ, a side's cause
506	        is the first event exclusive to that side whose changes contain
507	        ``key`` (zero deltas included) in that side's replay order, or
508	        ``None`` when no such event exists; when the values are equal,
509	        both causes are ``None``. ``path`` is the tuple of ids on the
510	        shortest parent-to-child path from the cause to that side's
511	        current head (both ends included), ties broken by the Unicode
512	        code point order of the complete id tuples, and ``affected`` is
513	        the tuple of the cause's strict descendant ids in that side's
514	        replay order; both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``.
515	        The query is read-only: the graph, branch heads and records are
516	        never modified, and the returned dict and tuples are detached
517	        from internal state.
518	        """
519	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
520	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
521	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
522	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
523	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
524	        if name_a == name_b:
525	            raise ValueError(
526	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
527	                "against itself"
528	            )
529	
530	        return self._attribute_divergence_for(
531	            self._heads[name_a], self._heads[name_b], key
532	        )

534	    def attribute_divergence_at(
535	        self,
536	        name_a: str,
537	        node_a: str,
538	        name_b: str,
539	        node_b: str,
540	        key: str,
541	    ) -> dict[str, object]:
542	        """Attribute the divergence of ``key`` at two historical nodes.
543	
544	        This is the historical-node form of :meth:`attribute_divergence`:
545	        instead of each branch's current head, the left side replays the
546	        ancestor closure of ``node_a`` on branch ``name_a`` and the right
547	        side that of ``node_b`` on branch ``name_b``. All five parameters
548	        are validated in signature order (``name_a``, ``node_a``,
549	        ``name_b``, ``node_b``, ``key``) before either node is replayed:
550	        non-``str`` values raise :class:`TypeError`, empty strings raise
551	        :class:`ValueError`; the branches are then looked up in order
552	        (``name_a`` first), an unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError`,
553	        and naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`; a
554	        node absent from the graph, or outside its named branch's current
555	        head ancestor closure (``node_a`` checked before ``node_b``),
556	        raises :class:`KeyError`.
557	
558	        Each node's ancestor closure is replayed in the graph's
559	        parents-before-children, ``(at, id)`` order; a side on which
560	        ``key`` never appears contributes the value ``0``. The result is
561	        a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``key, fork, left, right``:
562	        ``key`` is the queried key as given, ``fork`` is the last common
563	        event id in left replay order (or ``None`` when the closures
564	        share no event), and ``left``/``right`` are fresh dicts whose
565	        keys are ordered ``value, cause, path, affected``. When the two
566	        values differ, a side's cause is the first event exclusive to
567	        that side whose changes contain ``key`` (zero deltas included)
568	        in that side's replay order, or ``None`` when no such event
569	        exists; when the values are equal, both causes are ``None``.
570	        ``path`` is the tuple of ids on the shortest parent-to-child
571	        path from the cause to that side's node (both ends included),
572	        ties broken by the Unicode code point order of the complete id
573	        tuples, and ``affected`` is the tuple of the cause's strict
574	        descendant ids within that side's closure in its replay order;
575	        both are empty tuples when the cause is ``None``. The query is
576	        read-only: success or failure never modifies the graph, branch
577	        heads, audit or idempotency records, and the returned dict and
578	        tuples are detached from internal state.
579	        """
580	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
581	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
582	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
583	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
584	        self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
585	
586	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
587	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
588	        if name_a == name_b:
589	            raise ValueError(
590	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
591	                "against itself"
592	            )
593	
594	        if node_a not in self._graph._at:
595	            raise KeyError(node_a)
596	        if node_a not in set(
597	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
598	        ):
599	            raise KeyError(node_a)
600	        if node_b not in self._graph._at:
601	            raise KeyError(node_b)
602	        if node_b not in set(
603	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
604	        ):
605	            raise KeyError(node_b)

607	        return self._attribute_divergence_for(node_a, node_b, key)

609	    def attribute_divergences_at(
610	        self,
611	        name_a: str,
612	        node_a: str,
613	        name_b: str,
614	        node_b: str,
615	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
616	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
617	        """Attribute divergences for several keys at two historical nodes.
618	
619	        The multi-key form of :meth:`attribute_divergence_at`: all five
620	        parameters are validated before either node is replayed. The four
621	        string parameters are checked in signature order (``name_a``,
622	        ``node_a``, ``name_b``, ``node_b``): non-``str`` values raise
623	        :class:`TypeError` and empty strings raise :class:`ValueError`.
624	        ``keys`` must be a tuple (else :class:`TypeError`); its elements
625	        are checked in input order, and a non-``str`` element raises
626	        :class:`TypeError`, while an empty or duplicated key raises
627	        :class:`ValueError`. The branches are then looked up in order
628	        (``name_a`` first): an unknown branch raises :class:`KeyError` and
629	        naming the same branch twice raises :class:`ValueError`; a node
630	        absent from the graph, or outside its named branch's current head
631	        ancestor closure (``node_a`` checked before ``node_b``), raises
632	        :class:`KeyError`. Branch and node checks run even when ``keys``
633	        is empty, in which case an empty tuple is returned.
634	
635	        Every key is answered from one read-only historical view: both
636	        nodes' ancestor closures are taken once before results are built.
637	        The returned tuple has one fresh dict per key, ordered by the
638	        Unicode code point of the keys (independent of their input
639	        order); item-wise, each dict equals the result of
640	        :meth:`attribute_divergence_at` with the same first four
641	        arguments and that key, preserving its key order, types and full
642	        semantics. The dicts and tuples neither share objects with each
643	        other nor alias internal state. Success or failure never modifies
644	        the graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
645	        """
646	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
647	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
648	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
649	        self._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
650	        if not isinstance(keys, tuple):
651	            raise TypeError(
652	                f"keys must be a tuple, got {type(keys).__name__}"
653	            )
654	        seen_keys: set[str] = set()
655	        for key in keys:
656	            self._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
657	            if key in seen_keys:
658	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate key {key!r}")
659	            seen_keys.add(key)
660	
661	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
662	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
663	        if name_a == name_b:
664	            raise ValueError(
665	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
666	                "against itself"
667	            )
668	
669	        # Capture the read-only historical view before any node is
670	        # replayed: the branches' current head closures decide node
671	        # membership, and the nodes' own closures answer every key.
672	        head_closure_a = set(
673	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
674	        )
675	        head_closure_b = set(
676	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
677	        )
678	        if node_a not in self._graph._at or node_a not in head_closure_a:
679	            raise KeyError(node_a)
680	        if node_b not in self._graph._at or node_b not in head_closure_b:
681	            raise KeyError(node_b)
682	
683	        if not keys:
684	            return ()
685	
686	        left_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_a)
687	        right_order = self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_b)
688	        return tuple(
689	            self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(
690	                left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b, key
691	            )
692	            for key in sorted(keys)
693	        )

704	        The multi-point form of :meth:`attribute_divergences_at`:
705	        ``points`` is a tuple of ``(node_a, node_b)`` pairs, each played
706	        against the same two branches -- the left nodes live on

708	        ``name_b``'s.

711	        (``name_a``, ``name_b``, ``points``, ``keys``); containers are

756	                self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(

826	    def divergence_matrix(
827	        self,
828	        reference: str,

830	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
831	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
832	        """Run :meth:`divergence_summary` for several branches at once.
833	
834	        Each entry of ``series`` pairs a branch name with its own tuple of
835	        ``(reference node, series node)`` points, every point replayed
836	        against the same ``reference`` branch -- the left node must live on
837	        the reference branch's current head ancestor closure and the right
838	        node on the named series branch's.
839	
840	        ``reference`` is validated first: a non-``str`` value raises
841	        :class:`TypeError` and an empty string :class:`ValueError`.
842	        ``series`` must be a dict (else :class:`TypeError`); its keys are
843	        checked in insertion order, a non-``str`` series name raising
844	        :class:`TypeError` and an empty or ``reference``-equal name
845	        raising :class:`ValueError`, and each series' points are walked in
846	        input order. ``keys`` is checked last, exactly as in
847	        :meth:`divergence_summary`: it must be a tuple (else
848	        :class:`TypeError`), a non-``str`` element raises :class:`TypeError`,
849	        and an empty or duplicated key raises :class:`ValueError`. The rest
850	        of the validation, errors, empty-container handling and
851	        branch/node closure rules are exactly
852	        :meth:`divergence_summary`'s for the corresponding
853	        ``(reference, series_name, points, keys)`` call: points must be a
854	        tuple of length-2 node-id tuples with no repeated pair, and all
855	        inputs finish validating before the branches are looked up,
856	        reference first and then the series in ``series`` insertion order
857	        (unknown branch :class:`KeyError`, a node absent from the graph or
858	        the named branch's current head closure :class:`KeyError`, left
859	        before right, pairs in points order).
860

862	        historical view: the reference branch's and every series branch's
863	        current head closures and every node's own closure are taken once
864	        before results are built. The returned tuple follows ``series`` in
865	        its insertion order; each entry is a fresh dict whose keys are
866	        ordered ``branch, summaries, reconverged``: ``branch`` is the
867	        series branch name, ``summaries`` is the tuple of fresh summary
868	        dicts item-wise equal to :meth:`divergence_summary` for that series
869	        (keyed and ordered as there), and ``reconverged`` is a tuple of
870	        booleans aligned with ``summaries`` (keys in Unicode code point
871	        order) -- each is ``True`` exactly when the summary's
872	        ``first_diverged`` is not ``None`` and the two sides' values in its
873	        ``last`` attribution are equal. An empty ``series`` still
874	        validates ``reference`` and ``keys`` and looks the reference branch
875	        up, yielding an empty tuple; empty ``keys`` still validates every
876	        node, and each series then contributes empty
877	        ``summaries``/``reconverged`` tuples. The tuples and dicts at every
878	        level are freshly built, neither sharing objects with each other
879	        nor aliasing internal state. Success or failure never modifies the
880	        graph, branch heads, audit or idempotency records.
881	        """
882	        # --- All inputs finish validating before any branch is looked up,
883	        # mirroring divergence_summary's reference, branch, points, keys
884	        # order with series walked in insertion order. ---

964	    def rank_impacts(
965	        self,
966	        reference: str,
967	        series: dict[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]],

970	        """Rank branches by the weighted impact of their unconverged keys.
971

973	        entry of ``series`` pairs a branch name with its own tuple of
974	        ``(reference node, series node)`` points, replayed against the same
975	        ``reference`` branch exactly as there, and ``weights`` maps each
976	        examined state key to its non-negative weight.
977	
978	        ``reference`` and ``series`` are validated first, in exactly
979	        :meth:`divergence_matrix`'s order and with its errors: a
980	        non-``str`` or empty ``reference`` raises :class:`TypeError`/
981	        :class:`ValueError`; ``series`` must be a dict (else
982	        :class:`TypeError`); its keys are checked in insertion order, a
983	        non-``str`` series name raising :class:`TypeError` and an empty or
984	        ``reference``-equal name raising :class:`ValueError`; and each
985	        series' points are walked in input order (a non-tuple container or
986	        non-length-2-tuple point raises :class:`TypeError`, non-``str`` or
987	        empty node ids raise :class:`TypeError`/:class:`ValueError`, a
988	        repeated node pair raises :class:`ValueError`). ``weights`` is
989	        checked last, before any branch is looked up: it must be a dict
990	        (else :class:`TypeError`); its entries are walked in insertion
991	        order, a non-``str`` key raising :class:`TypeError` and an empty
992	        key raising :class:`ValueError`; each weight must be a non-``bool``
993	        :class:`int` or :class:`float` (anything else raises
994	        :class:`TypeError`), and a negative, NaN or infinite weight raises
995	        :class:`ValueError`. The branches are then looked up, reference
996	        first and then the series in ``series`` insertion order (unknown
997	        branch :class:`KeyError`), and nodes are checked per pair, left
998	        before right, pairs in points order (:class:`KeyError` when absent
999	        from the graph or the named branch's current head closure).
1000	
1001	        Every series, point and key is answered from one shared read-only
1002	        historical view: the reference branch's and every series branch's
1003	        current head closures and every node's own closure are taken once
1004	        before results are built. For each series branch the examined
1005	        keys are the ``weights`` keys, ordered by Unicode code point; their
1006	        per-point divergences and final attributions are item-wise equal
1007	        to :meth:`divergence_summary`'s for the same arguments. Each branch
1008	        contributes a fresh dict whose keys are ordered ``branch, score,
1009	        first_impact, unconverged, attributions``:
1010	
1011	        ``score`` is the sum, over the keys whose left and right replayed
1012	        values still differ at the final point, of the absolute value
1013	        difference times the key's weight -- plain Python arithmetic
1014	        yielding an :class:`int` or :class:`float` with no rounding, and a
1015	        zero result is never negative zero. ``first_impact`` is the
1016	        smallest ``first_diverged`` point index among the keys that
1017	        diverged at least once, or ``None`` when no examined key ever
1018	        diverged. ``unconverged`` is the tuple of the still-diverging keys
1019	        ordered by Unicode code point, and ``attributions`` aligns with it:
1020	        one fresh ``key, fork, left, right`` attribution dict per
1021	        unconverged key, item-wise equal to that key's ``last`` attribution
1022	        in :meth:`divergence_matrix`.
1023	
1024	        The rows are sorted by descending ``score``, then ascending
1025	        ``first_impact`` with ``None`` placed after every integer, then by
1026	        the Unicode code point of the branch name. An empty ``series``
1027	        still validates ``reference`` and ``weights`` and looks the
1028	        reference branch up, yielding an empty tuple; empty ``weights``
1029	        still validates every branch and node, and each series then
1030	        contributes a zero score, ``None`` and empty ``unconverged`` and
1031	        ``attributions`` tuples. The tuples and dicts at every level are
1032	        freshly built, neither sharing objects with each other nor aliasing
1033	        internal state. Success or failure never modifies the graph,
1034	        branch heads, audit or idempotency records.

1036	        # --- All inputs finish validating before any branch is looked up,
1037	        # mirroring divergence_matrix with weights in the keys position. ---
1038	        self._require_nonempty_str(reference, "reference")
1039	        if not isinstance(series, dict):
1040	            raise TypeError(
1041	                f"series must be a dict, got {type(series).__name__}"
1042	            )
1043	        per_series: list[tuple[str, tuple[tuple[str, str], ...]]] = []
1044	        for series_name, series_points in series.items():
1045	            self._require_nonempty_str(series_name, "series branch")
1046	            if series_name == reference:
1047	                raise ValueError(
1048	                    f"series branch {series_name!r} cannot equal reference "
1049	                    f"branch {reference!r}"
1050	                )

1052	            per_series.append((series_name, series_points))
1053	        ordered_keys = self._validate_weights(weights)
1054	
1055	        self._require_known_branch(reference)
1056	
1057	        # Capture the shared read-only view before any result is built,
1058	        # exactly as in divergence_matrix.
1059	        reference_head_closure = set(
1060	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[reference])
1061	        )
1062	        views: list[
1063	            tuple[str, list[tuple[list[str], list[str], str, str]] | None]
1064	        ] = []
1065	        for series_name, series_points in per_series:
1066	            self._require_known_branch(series_name)
1067	            head_closure_b = set(
1068	                self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[series_name])
1069	            )
1070	            for node_a, node_b in series_points:
1071	                if (
1072	                    node_a not in self._graph._at
1073	                    or node_a not in reference_head_closure
1074	                ):
1075	                    raise KeyError(node_a)
1076	                if (
1077	                    node_b not in self._graph._at
1078	                    or node_b not in head_closure_b
1079	                ):
1080	                    raise KeyError(node_b)
1081	            ordered_points: list[
1082	                tuple[list[str], list[str], str, str]
1083	            ] | None = None
1084	            if series_points:
1085	                ordered_points = [
1086	                    (
1087	                        self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_a),
1088	                        self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_b),
1089	                        node_a,
1090	                        node_b,
1091	                    )
1092	                    for node_a, node_b in series_points
1093	                ]
1094	            views.append((series_name, ordered_points))
1095	
1096	        rows: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1097	        for series_name, ordered_points in views:
1098	            summaries = self._divergence_summaries(
1099	                ordered_points, ordered_keys
1100	            )
1101	            unconverged: list[str] = []
1102	            attributions: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1103	            diverged_indices: list[int] = []
1104	            score: int | float = 0
1105	            for summary in summaries:
1106	                first_diverged = summary["first_diverged"]
1107	                if first_diverged is not None:
1108	                    diverged_indices.append(first_diverged)
1109	                last = summary["last"]
1110	                left_value = last["left"]["value"]
1111	                right_value = last["right"]["value"]
1112	                if left_value == right_value:

1114	                key = summary["key"]

1119	            if score == 0:

1121	            rows.append(
1122	                {
1123	                    "branch": series_name,
1124	                    "score": score,
1125	                    "first_impact": (
1126	                        min(diverged_indices) if diverged_indices else None
1127	                    ),
1128	                    "unconverged": tuple(unconverged),
1129	                    "attributions": tuple(attributions),
1130	                }
1131	            )
1132	        rows.sort(
1133	            key=lambda row: (
1134	                -row["score"],
1135	                row["first_impact"] is None,
1136	                (
1137	                    row["first_impact"]

1139	                    else 0
1140	                ),

1147	    def _validate_weights(weights: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
1148	        """Validate ``weights`` and return its keys in Unicode order.
1149	
1150	        The weight-map counterpart of :meth:`_validate_keys`: a non-dict
1151	        raises :class:`TypeError`; entries are walked in insertion order,
1152	        a non-``str`` key raising :class:`TypeError` and an empty key
1153	        raising :class:`ValueError`; each weight must be a non-``bool``
1154	        :class:`int` or :class:`float` (else :class:`TypeError`) and must
1155	        not be negative, NaN or infinite (else :class:`ValueError`).
1156	        """
1157	        if not isinstance(weights, dict):
1158	            raise TypeError(
1159	                f"weights must be a dict, got {type(weights).__name__}"
1160	            )
1161	        for key, value in weights.items():
1162	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "weight key")
1163	            if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, (int, float)):
1164	                raise TypeError(
1165	                    f"weight for {key!r} must be an int or float, got "
1166	                    f"{type(value).__name__}"
1167	                )
1168	            if isinstance(value, float) and (
1169	                math.isnan(value) or math.isinf(value)
1170	            ):
1171	                raise ValueError(f"weight for {key!r} must be finite")
1172	            if value < 0:

1200	    @staticmethod
1201	    def _validate_points(points: Any) -> None:
1202	        """Validate a tuple of length-2, unique node-id pairs.
1203	
1204	        Shared by :meth:`divergence_timeline`, :meth:`divergence_summary`
1205	        and :meth:`divergence_matrix` so points raise identical errors: a
1206	        non-tuple container or non-length-2-tuple point raises
1207	        :class:`TypeError`, non-``str`` or empty node ids raise
1208	        :class:`TypeError`/:class:`ValueError` (left node before right),
1209	        and a repeated node pair raises :class:`ValueError`.
1210	        """
1211	        if not isinstance(points, tuple):
1212	            raise TypeError(
1213	                f"points must be a tuple, got {type(points).__name__}"
1214	            )
1215	        seen_points: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()
1216	        for point in points:
1217	            if not isinstance(point, tuple) or len(point) != 2:
1218	                raise TypeError(
1219	                    "each point must be a length-2 tuple of node ids, "
1220	                    f"got {point!r} ({type(point).__name__})"
1221	                )
1222	            node_a, node_b = point
1223	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(node_a, "node_a")
1224	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(node_b, "node_b")
1225	            pair = (node_a, node_b)
1226	            if pair in seen_points:
1227	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate point {pair!r}")
1228	            seen_points.add(pair)

1230	    @staticmethod
1231	    def _validate_keys(keys: Any) -> tuple[str, ...]:
1232	        """Validate ``keys`` and return them in Unicode code point order.
1233	
1234	        Shared by the divergence family: a non-tuple raises
1235	        :class:`TypeError`, a non-``str`` element raises :class:`TypeError`,
1236	        and an empty or duplicated key raises :class:`ValueError`. Summary
1237	        and matrix rows always present keys by Unicode code point, so the
1238	        sorted, duplicate-free tuple is returned once.
1239	        """
1240	        if not isinstance(keys, tuple):
1241	            raise TypeError(
1242	                f"keys must be a tuple, got {type(keys).__name__}"
1243	            )
1244	        seen_keys: set[str] = set()
1245	        for key in keys:
1246	            EventGraph._require_nonempty_str(key, "key")
1247	            if key in seen_keys:
1248	                raise ValueError(f"duplicate key {key!r}")
1249	            seen_keys.add(key)
1250	        return tuple(sorted(keys))

1252	    def _divergence_inputs(
1253	        self,
1254	        name_a: str,
1255	        name_b: str,
1256	        points: tuple[tuple[str, str], ...],
1257	        keys: tuple[str, ...],
1258	    ) -> tuple[
1259	        list[tuple[list[str], list[str], str, str]] | None,
1260	        tuple[str, ...],
1261	    ]:
1262	        """Validate and capture the single read-only divergence view.
1263	
1264	        Shared by :meth:`divergence_timeline` and
1265	        :meth:`divergence_summary` so both apply identical validation
1266	        order, errors, empty-container handling and branch/node closure
1267	        rules, and answer every point and key from one historical view.
1268	        Returns the keys in Unicode code point order alongside a list of
1269	        one ``(left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b)`` entry per point
1270	        in input order; the list is ``None`` when ``points`` is empty (the
1271	        empty-tuple result case).
1272	        """
1273	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_a, "name_a")
1274	        self._require_nonempty_str(name_b, "name_b")
1275	        self._validate_points(points)
1276	        ordered_keys = self._validate_keys(keys)
1277	
1278	        self._require_known_branch(name_a)
1279	        self._require_known_branch(name_b)
1280	        if name_a == name_b:
1281	            raise ValueError(
1282	                f"cannot attribute divergence for branch {name_a!r} "
1283	                "against itself"
1284	            )
1285	
1286	        if not points:
1287	            return None, ordered_keys
1288	
1289	        # Capture the single read-only historical view: the current head
1290	        # closures decide node membership for every pair, and the nodes'
1291	        # own closures answer every key.
1292	        head_closure_a = set(
1293	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_a])
1294	        )
1295	        head_closure_b = set(
1296	            self._graph._ordered_ancestors(self._heads[name_b])
1297	        )
1298	        for node_a, node_b in points:
1299	            if node_a not in self._graph._at or node_a not in head_closure_a:
1300	                raise KeyError(node_a)
1301	            if node_b not in self._graph._at or node_b not in head_closure_b:
1302	                raise KeyError(node_b)
1303	
1304	        return [
1305	            (
1306	                self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_a),
1307	                self._graph._ordered_ancestors(node_b),
1308	                node_a,
1309	                node_b,
1310	            )
1311	            for node_a, node_b in points
1312	        ], ordered_keys

1314	    def _divergence_summaries(
1315	        self,
1316	        ordered_points: list[tuple[list[str], list[str], str, str]]
1317	        | None,
1318	        ordered_keys: tuple[str, ...],
1319	    ) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
1320	        """Build :meth:`divergence_summary` rows from a captured view.
1321	
1322	        ``ordered_points`` is one captured view entry per point in input
1323	        order, or ``None``/empty when there are no points; ``ordered_keys``
1324	        are already sorted by Unicode code point. Shared by
1325	        :meth:`divergence_summary` and :meth:`divergence_matrix`, so a
1326	        matrix row is item-wise equal to the corresponding standalone
1327	        summary call. With no points or keys an empty tuple is returned.
1328	        """
1329	        if not ordered_points or not ordered_keys:
1330	            return ()
1331	
1332	        # All attributes per (point, key) come from the captured view.
1333	        attributed: list[dict[str, dict[str, Any]]] = [
1334	            {
1335	                key: self._attribute_divergence_on_orders(
1336	                    left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b, key
1337	                )
1338	                for key in ordered_keys
1339	            }
1340	            for left_order, right_order, node_a, node_b in ordered_points
1341	        ]
1342	
1343	        summaries: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1344	        for key in ordered_keys:
1345	            first_diverged: int | None = None
1346	            transitions: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1347	            prev_diverged: bool | None = None
1348	            prev_left_cause: object = None
1349	            prev_right_cause: object = None
1350	            for index, per_key in enumerate(attributed):
1351	                record = per_key[key]
1352	                left = record["left"]
1353	                right = record["right"]
1354	                left_value = left["value"]
1355	                right_value = right["value"]
1356	                left_cause = left["cause"]
1357	                right_cause = right["cause"]
1358	                diverged = left_value != right_value
1359	                if diverged and first_diverged is None:
1360	                    first_diverged = index
1361	
1362	                kind: str | None = None
1363	                if prev_diverged is None:
1364	                    if diverged:
1365	                        kind = "diverged"
1366	                elif not prev_diverged and diverged:
1367	                    kind = "diverged"
1368	                elif prev_diverged and not diverged:
1369	                    kind = "converged"
1370	                elif (
1371	                    prev_diverged
1372	                    and diverged
1373	                    and (
1374	                        prev_left_cause != left_cause
1375	                        or prev_right_cause != right_cause
1376	                    )
1377	                ):
1378	                    kind = "reattributed"
1379	                if kind is not None:
1380	                    transitions.append(
1381	                        {
1382	                            "index": index,
1383	                            "kind": kind,
1384	                            "left_value": left_value,
1385	                            "right_value": right_value,
1386	                            "left_cause": left_cause,
1387	                            "right_cause": right_cause,
1388	                        }
1389	                    )
1390	
1391	                prev_diverged = diverged
1392	                prev_left_cause = left_cause
1393	                prev_right_cause = right_cause
1394	
1395	            summaries.append(
1396	                {
1397	                    "key": key,
1398	                    "first_diverged": first_diverged,
1399	                    "transitions": tuple(transitions),
1400	                    "last": self._copy_attribution(attributed[-1][key]),
1401	                }
1402	            )
1403	        return tuple(summaries)

1421	    def _attribute_divergence_on_orders(
